text: July the twenty-third, nineteen eighty-three. Air Canada Flight one forty-three is getting ready to fly from Montreal to Edmonton. The seven sixty-seven is one of the airline's newest planes, and one of the first to measure its fuel in kilograms instead of pounds. But tonight, the fuel gauges in the cockpit are blank. A faulty sensor has knocked them out. By the rules, the plane should never have been cleared to fly. But it was. So the crew does it the old way. A stick is dipped into the tanks, the depth is read, and a chart turns it into litres.
